h1: Budget-Friendly Playground Equipment Options for Schools in India

props.title: Budget-Friendly Playground Equipment Options for Schools in India
props.summaryText: How to get the most play out of a limited school budget: which equipment gives the best value per child, where you can save, where you should not, and how to phase the project.
props.author: ananya-kulkarni
props.imageAlt: Close-up of colourful slides and climbing panels on a school play structure

takeaways.text: Measure value as play per child, not price per item: one well-chosen structure can keep a whole class busy.
Ground-level equipment such as hopping posts, balance beams and play panels is cheap and adds a lot of play.
Save on themes and custom colours before you save on steel, plastic or surfacing.
Phase the project and leave space and foundations for later additions.
Ask alumni, parent associations and CSR partners to fund named phases.

faq.q: What is the cheapest playground equipment for schools?
faq.a: Individual items such as spring riders, see-saws, balancing beams, hopping posts and play panels cost far less than large structures and add a lot of play. A compact multi play station gives the most play per rupee for a whole class.

faq.q: How can a school fund a new playground?
faq.a: Phase the project, and approach parent associations, alumni, local businesses and company CSR programmes to fund named phases such as a toddler zone or a swing set. Some schools add one new item each academic year.

faq.q: Is it safe to buy second-hand playground equipment?
faq.a: It is risky. You rarely know the age, condition or standard of second-hand equipment, spares may not be available, and dismantling and moving it can damage it. If you consider it, have it inspected by a qualified person first.

faq.q: Where should a school not cut costs on a playground?
faq.a: On safety surfacing under the equipment, on the quality of steel, plastic and coatings, and on proper foundations and installation. These decide whether the playground is safe and still usable after five years.
